findings.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — P1, confidence 100: `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` writes a sorted set into existing `span-buf:s:*` keys that pre-deploy workers created as Redis sets, so a rolling deployment receives WRONGTYPE on every affected span batch and stops span-buffer ingestion until the old keys expire.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1, confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` applies numeric rounding to the `AuditLogEntry.datetime` value selected by the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, so every authorized `optimized_pagination=true` audit-log request with at least one row raises TypeError while constructing its cursor.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:68 (`if span_count > 1000 then`) — [P1, confidence 100] The new insertion-time eviction requirement has no boundary or score-order test, so a regression that retains more than 1000 spans or removes the newest spans ships undetected.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1; confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError when the opted-in audit-log paginator builds its cursor from the `datetime` selected by `order_by="-datetime"`, so authorized administrators receive a 500 instead of a page.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — [P1; confidence 100] `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` raises Django's `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` whenever the advertised negative-offset cursor path is used, so the enabled advanced pagination request fails rather than navigating backward.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — [P1, confidence 100] The added `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` branch changes the public audit-log API and paginator behavior even though the accepted task only authorizes optimizing spans-buffer insertion with eviction, so the final artifact no longer preserves its stated objective.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1; confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on an `AuditLogEntry.datetime`, so every authorized `optimized_pagination=true` request that returns an audit-log row raises `TypeError` and returns a 500.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — [P1, confidence 100] The added `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` audit-log pagination feature is unrelated to the stated spans-buffer insertion-and-eviction task, expanding the change into a separate public API behavior without a traceable requirement.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:181 — [P1, confidence 100] The changed `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` alters the shared paginator's behavior for every reverse-cursor endpoint even though the stated task is limited to spans-buffer insertion eviction, so unrelated API behavior ships in this change.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:818 — [P1, confidence 100] The new `class OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator):` introduces a general audit-log pagination abstraction outside the spans-buffer task boundary, making the review and deployment scope materially broader than the stated intent.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — [P1, confidence 100] The new eviction branch `if span_count > 1000 then` has no test with more than 1,000 differently scored spans, so a regression that retains the oldest spans, evicts the wrong count, or never evicts ships while every updated four-span fixture passes.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — [P1, confidence 100] The new request-controlled branch `if use_optimized and enable_advanced:` has no corresponding endpoint or paginator test, so a regression in flag parsing, administrator gating, or `OptimizedCursorPaginator` response behavior ships undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — P1, confidence 100: `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` writes a sorted set into existing `span-buf:s:*` keys that pre-deploy workers created as Redis sets, so a rolling deployment receives WRONGTYPE on every affected span batch and stops span-buffer ingestion until the old keys expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a change from Redis SET operations (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to SORTED SET operations (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) for the same keys (span-buf:s:*). During a rolling deployment, old workers would have created these keys as regular sets, while new workers will try to use sorted set commands on them. Redis will return WRONGTYPE errors when sorted set commands are executed against keys that are regular sets, causing span buffer ingestion failures until the old keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:68 (`if span_count > 1000 then`) — [P1, confidence 100] The new insertion-time eviction requirement has no boundary or score-order test, so a regression that retains more than 1000 spans or removes the newest spans ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new eviction logic in add-buffer.lua (lines 57-60) that limits spans to 1000 using zpopmin. The finding correctly identifies that the test files (test_buffer.py, test_flusher.py, test_consumer.py) don't include any tests verifying this new 1000-span limit behavior or that zpopmin removes the oldest spans (lowest scores) rather than newest. This is a legitimate missing test concern for newly added nontrivial logic - the eviction behavior could regress without detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1; confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError when the opted-in audit-log paginator builds its cursor from the `datetime` selected by `order_by="-datetime"`, so authorized administrators receive a 500 instead of a page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 840 calls math.floor(value) or math.ceil(value) on the result of getattr(item, self.key). When used with order_by='-datetime' in the audit log endpoint (line 77), self.key would be 'datetime', meaning value would be a datetime object. Calling math.floor() or math.ceil() on a datetime raises TypeError since these functions require numeric types. This is a real bug that would cause 500 errors for administrators using the optimized pagination feature.
